Header.CaseTitle: Sterling Investments Ltd v Blackwood Capital Partners LLP

Counsel.Lead: Michael Taylor KC; Sarah Clarke (instructed by Freshfields Bruckhaus Deringer LLP)

SummaryOfPosition.Summary: The Appellant seeks damages for breach of an investment management agreement, contending that the Respondent failed to exercise reasonable skill and care in managing a £45 million portfolio, resulting in losses of approximately £12 million.

FactsReliedOn.item: The Appellant entered into an Investment Management Agreement with the Respondent dated 15 March 2018.
The Agreement required the Respondent to manage the portfolio with reasonable skill and care appropriate to a professional investment manager.
Between September 2019 and March 2020, the Respondent concentrated 40% of the portfolio in technology sector derivatives contrary to the agreed risk parameters.
The Appellant suffered losses of £12.3 million when the technology sector experienced significant correction in Q1 2020.
Despite requests, the Respondent failed to provide adequate documentation of its investment rationale.

Contentions.item: The Respondent breached its duty of care by failing to diversify the portfolio adequately.
The concentration in technology derivatives exceeded the risk parameters agreed in the Investment Management Agreement.
The Respondent failed to conduct adequate due diligence before making the investments complained of.
The losses were caused by the Respondent's breach of duty and not by unforeseeable market conditions.

LegalBasis.item: Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, s.138D

ReliefSought.item: Interest pursuant to s.35A Senior Courts Act 1981

AuthoritiesCited.Authority: Hedley Byrne & Co Ltd v Heller & Partners Ltd [1964] AC 465
Henderson v Merrett Syndicates Ltd [1995] 2 AC 145
Rubenstein v HSBC Bank plc [2012] EWCA Civ 1184
